_comment: Accepted GuardDog threat-* findings on our own dependencies.
GuardDog splits its rules three ways. capability-* is descriptive ('this
package can read files') and fires on virtually every real library, so
the gate ignores it entirely -- a gate that shouts about aiohttp making
network requests would be turned off within a week. threat-* and the
metadata heuristics (typosquatting, compromised maintainer email) are
the ones that mean something, and those are what this gate enforces.
Each entry below is a threat-* rule that fires on a package we already
depend on, with the reason it is accepted. Anything NOT listed here
fails the build. Entries may be removed, never added, without a note.
This is a ratchet, not a mute button: the pair (package, rule) is what
is accepted, so the same rule firing on a DIFFERENT package is still a

psutil.threat-process-memory: psutil's entire purpose is reading process and memory information; the rule detects exactly the API surface the library is built on.

idna.threat-runtime-obfuscation-unicode: idna implements the international domain name standard, so its tables are full of homoglyphs and uncommon codepoints by definition.
